audits.title: Introduction of ECT Discharge Summary- a Quality Improvement Project to Improve Communication Between Treating and Referring Clinicians and Aiming Better Patient Care
audits.setting: Mid Essex ECT clinic, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Legal status documented 5%; written consent/Form 5 95%; Mini-ACE 5%; MADRS 0%.

audits.intervention: Checklists and assessments introduced after an earlier QIP, then ECT discharge summaries generated for every patient from November 2021.

cycle2.result: Legal status, written consent/Form 5, Mini-ACE and MADRS all 100% (excluding patients who did not complete treatment).

audits.other_findings: Discharge summaries improved communication with referring clinicians and patient and carer satisfaction.
audits.citation: Ahmad A, Khan A, Abiodun Y. Introduction of ECT Discharge Summary- a Quality Improvement Project to Improve Communication Between Treating and Referring Clinicians and Aiming Better Patient Care. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(S1):S80-S81. doi:10.1192/bjo.2022.264.

audits.title: Audit Reviewing Consent for Electro Convulsive Therapy
audits.standard: NICE ECT guidance on valid consent and Mental Health Act (Scotland) forms T2, T3A and T4

cycle1.result: Over 30% of cases lacked the documentation proposed by NICE; of cases with complete documentation, 25% were informal and 75% under the Mental Health Act.

audits.intervention: Planned: dissemination to prescribing consultants and redesign of the ECT booklet to include required documents.
audits.citation: Ansari S, Maiya S. Audit Reviewing Consent for Electro Convulsive Therapy. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(S1):S84-S84. doi:10.1192/bjo.2022.271.

audits.title: A Clinical Audit of ECT Documentation in NHS Grampian
audits.standard: NICE guidance on ECT: documented risk/benefit assessment including anaesthetic risk and cognitive impairment, patient information leaflet, consultation of advocate

cycle1.result: Indication documented 100%; RCPsych leaflet received 50%; risk/benefit discussion documented 50%; specific side effects discussed 50%

audits.other_findings: Standardised consent form being considered, with re-audit planned after introduction.
audits.citation: Ball R, Smith M. A Clinical Audit of ECT Documentation in NHS Grampian. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S217-S218. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.538.

audits.title: Audit of Electroconvulsive Therapy Service Provision in Lincolnshire Partnership Foundation Trust: Current Standards and Adherence to National Guidance
audits.standard: NICE guidance and ECT accreditation service standards (indication, consent, monitoring)
audits.setting: ECT clinic, Lincolnshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Pre-ECT assessment documented 70%; consent by psychiatrist 70%; baseline CGI/CPRS 20%; baseline MADRS 40% with no weekly monitoring; baseline MoCA 100% but not repeated every four treatments; under a quarter had post-ECT clinician review.

audits.other_findings: Ongoing consent was not reviewed at each treatment. Revision of the local ECT record pathway by December 2023 and re-audit in March 2024 recommended.
audits.citation: Kyaw S, Butt A, Priya A, Kunigiri G, Kumar P. Audit of Electroconvulsive Therapy Service Provision in Lincolnshire Partnership Foundation Trust: Current Standards and Adherence to National Guidance. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S246-S247. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.598.

audits.title: From Baseline to Recovery: An Audit of Pre- and Post-ECT (Electro Convulsive Therapy) Patient Assessments
audits.standard: Scottish ECT Accreditation Network (SEAN) standards: MoCA, MADRS and CGI before, after and at 3 and 6 months after ECT

cycle1.result: Pre-ECT MoCA 20/32, MADRS 28, CGI 26; post-ECT MoCA 10, MADRS 11, CGI 13; no 3- or 6-month follow-up assessments.

audits.other_findings: Recommended robust processes and specialist nurse-led clinics for post-ECT follow-up assessments.
audits.citation: Ansari S, Maiya S. From Baseline to Recovery: An Audit of Pre- and Post-ECT (Electro Convulsive Therapy) Patient Assessments. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S117-S117. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10335.

audits.title: Audit of Electroconvulsive Therapy (ECT) Service Provision: Current Practices and Adherence to Guidelines at Punjab Institute of Mental Health, Lahore, Pakistan
audits.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists ECT guidelines (consent, vital signs, monitoring of clinical response and cognitive side effects)
audits.setting: Punjab Institute of Mental Health, Lahore

cycle1.result: Consent forms completed 100% and ongoing consent checked for all; right to withdraw consent explained to none; vital signs robustly documented; no validated rating scale used; response between sessions assessed in 45%; no documentation of cognitive side-effect assessment.

audits.intervention: Recommended updating consent forms to include right to withdraw, culturally validated assessment tools and re-audit in one year.
audits.citation: Sheikh M, Irfan A, Sarwar A, Ahmed M, Ali H. Audit of Electroconvulsive Therapy (ECT) Service Provision: Current Practices and Adherence to Guidelines at Punjab Institute of Mental Health, Lahore, Pakistan. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S276-S277. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10673.

audits.title: Evaluating Adherence to National Standards: A Two-Year Audit of Consent, Clinical Efficacy, and Longitudinal Monitoring in Electroconvulsive Therapy
audits.standard: ECT Accreditation Service (ECTAS) standards for consent, capacity and monitoring of target symptoms and cognitive side effects
audits.setting: ECT service, Sheffield Health Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Legal framework and consent documentation met standards; baseline monitoring 100% for all measures, falling below 75% by course completion and declining further at months two and three of follow-up.

audits.other_findings: Compliance was similar to previous local and national audits; inpatients had more missing data (11.5 vs 8.2). Mean MADRS fell from 42.1 to 21.3 and mini-ACE rose from 19.7 to 23.9 (p<0.01).
audits.citation: Scott-Bridge K, Ruwizhu T, Nyan N, Blackburn A, Sivakumar V. Evaluating Adherence to National Standards: A Two-Year Audit of Consent, Clinical Efficacy, and Longitudinal Monitoring in Electroconvulsive Therapy. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S13-S13. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11175.

audits.title: Re-Audit of Documentation Practices in the Blossomwood Electroconvulsive Therapy Suite Using a Quality Improvement Approach
audits.setting: Blossomwood ECT suite, Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 100% compliance in 15 of 20 criteria; MADRS 71.4%, MINI-ACE 85.7%, previous treatment failure 85.7%.

audits.other_findings: Titled a re-audit but only one set of results given; root causes were limited awareness, non-mandatory templates, unclear policy and paper systems.
audits.citation: Kadri O, Krishnan D, Rajendram M. Re-Audit of Documentation Practices in the Blossomwood Electroconvulsive Therapy Suite Using a Quality Improvement Approach. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S164-S164. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11406.
